news.title: Thomas Müller recounts Germany’s 7-1 win against Brazil in the 2014 World Cup
news.lede: Thomas Müller is never going to retire, is he? The Bayern Munich legend and Vancouver Whitecaps attacker recently featured on an episode of the Late Run podcast. In the episode, they look back at his career, and one of the main talking points was Germany’s incredible run in the 2014 World Cup and their ultimate victory. Specifically, Müller provided a behind-the-scenes look at their famous 7-1 win against Brazil.

news.title: Matildas bring World Cup build-up to Geelong
news.lede: Football Australia executive director of football Heather Garriock. Photo: Asanka Ratnayake/Getty Images. Geelong football fans will get another chance to cheer on the Matildas at home when Australia takes on Colombia at Kardinia Park this December. The 2 December clash will bring international women’s football back to the city, two years after more than 30,000 supporters watched the Matildas defeat Chinese Taipei 6–0 at the same venue.

news.title: Copper Princesses goalkeepers sharpen reflexes ahead of World Cup
news.lede: Zambia’s Copper Princesses continued their preparations for the FIFA Under-17 Women’s World Cup with a focused goalkeeping session in Casablanca on Tuesday. Goalkeeper coach Danny Mbao put the team’s three goalkeepers — Bukata Kakumbi, Winfridah Mutale and Decent Mbewe — through their paces at the Club Sportif Academie des Electricienes de Football. The trio worked on their reflexes and reactions as Zambia stepped up preparations for the World Cup, which begins in Morocco later this month. Despite the demands of a long-haul journey, the goalkeepers completed a full training session as the technical bench continued to fine-tune the squad ahead of the tournament.

news.title: A new equation shocks the football world: Yamal breaks the Messi and Cristiano barrier
news.lede: How did Lamine prove he is better than "the Flea" and "the Don"? In an era obsessed with numbers, Barcelona's gifted Lamine Yamal has chosen to answer the doubters in a language only the greats understand: consistency and impact. The 19-year-old is no longer merely a promising talent. He has become an unprecedented goalscoring phenomenon, achieving what Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo, Kylian Mbappé and Erling Haaland could not at the same age.

news.title: Gianni Infantino under pressure over new World Cup scandal after 'allowing ineligible player'
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has come under yet more scrutiny after it was reported that FIFA knowingly allowed an ineligible player to play for DR Congo in a crucial World Cup qualifier. Congo made a mark at the World Cup in the summer, reaching the knockout stages, where they gave England a scare in a competitive 2-1 come-from-behind win for Thomas Tuchel's side in the last 32. One of their stars in that match was goalkeeper Lionel Mpasi, who has now found himself at the centre of an eligibility scandal. As first reported by The New York Times , FIFA knew that Congo hadn't completed the paperwork for Mpasi to switch his international allegiance from France to the African nation before they played, and beat, Jamaica in a World Cup qualification play-off in March.
